text:
The Senators are 10-6-1 with 21 points, and the goal differential is perfectly flat: 52 scored, 52 allowed. Our numbers have them at 51% of the expected goals, with goals and chances lined up almost exactly at both ends. That's a solid, unspectacular team that has won a few more close games than it lost, about two points' worth by our count.

The latest was a 2-1 regulation win in Buffalo on Nov. 4 to finish a five-game road trip, with Michael Amadio scoring the winner inside the last three minutes. Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe wrote that Amadio "feels like he should have 10+ goals already this season." Ersson held off the late Sabres push.

The forward lines haven't settled. The most-used trio (Claude Giroux, Amadio and Shane Pinto) has only 57 minutes together and sits at 47% of the chances. The most promising look is Giroux with Tim Stützle and Fabian Zetterlund: 76% of the expected goals in 41 minutes, a small sample worth more of. The team's own video calls it a "Different Level This Year" for Stützle.

On defence, Thomas Chabot and Jordan Spence have been the engine (60%, 9-6 in goals). Ottawa plays a lot of special teams, drawing 5.35 penalties a game and taking 4.88, with a penalty kill that allows 0.87 expected goals a night. Our numbers give the Senators 67% playoff odds on a 97-point pace.
headline: Ottawa keeps winning the close ones
